newsitem.title: USA: Mars probe heads for the Red Planet.
newsitem.headline: Mars probe heads for the Red Planet.

text.p: A U.S. Mars probe blasted off from Florida on Thursday, beginning a 10-month interplanetary voyage to the Red Planet.
The Mars Global Surveyor soared aloft at 12:00 p.m. EST (1700 GMT) atop a McDonnell Douglas Corp. Delta 2 rocket launched from Cape Canaveral Air Station.

NASA had just 20 days to get the probe off the launch pad or faced a wait of 25 months for the planets to realign. Thursday's launch was one day late because the takeoff was delayed from Wednesday because of bad weather.
The spacecraft was designed and built in record time to replace NASA's $1 billion Mars Observer probe which was lost in 1993 just days before it was due to enter orbit about the Red Planet.
Surveyor carries indentical copies of five of the seven scientific instruments on its ill-fated predecessor, but at $215 million is much cheaper.

The probe is due to slip into an egg-shapped orbit around Mars on September 12 next year. It will lower and circularize its orbit by dipping into the thin Martian atmosphere and using its wing-like solar panels as air brakes.
